title: Let's Build It Again
can_do: 不小心碰倒同伴的积木后，先关心同伴并道歉，再征得同意一起重新搭好。

conversation_move.label: apologize and repair the shared activity

trigger: Child accidentally knocks the upper two blocks from Peer's tower; he apologizes, checks on Peer, and they rebuild it in the same color order.
setting: Child and the same Bear Peer from the cooperation chapter kneel beside a small block tower on a home play mat.
essential_props: one three-block tower: a tan base, a blue middle block and a red top block

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: Oops! Your blocks fell. I'm sorry.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.line: I'm okay. But my tower is gone.

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: I can help build it again. The tan block is the base.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.line: Yes! You hold the base. I'll stack the blue and red.

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: Okay. I'll hold it very steady.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.line: Blue in the middle, red on top.

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: There. Tall again. I'm glad you're okay.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.line: Me too. Building together is fun.

replay_cards.title: Fix the drawing
replay_cards.setting: Child and Bear Peer draw on a shared sheet
replay_cards.change: Child's crayon accidentally crosses the road Peer was drawing
replay_cards.challenge: Child stops drawing, notices the crossed road and says "I'm sorry. Are you okay?" Peer says he is okay but wanted a clear road. Child asks how to help; Peer suggests making the accidental line a bridge. Child asks before adding the two bridge edges, Peer agrees, and they connect the repaired road together. Peer may still look disappointed.

replay_cards.title: Return the moved piece
replay_cards.setting: A shared puzzle with Bear Peer
replay_cards.change: Child takes a piece Peer had set beside an empty space, thinking it was unused
replay_cards.challenge: Peer explains that he was about to place that piece. Child apologizes and offers "I can put it back." Peer agrees and Child returns it to the same spot, leaving Peer to fit it himself. Child then asks "Can I play with you?" Peer asks him to find a corner piece, and they resume with separate useful jobs.

parent_support: Keep the accidental damage visible so concern and the apology have a real cause. Child speaks sincerely and calmly; do not demand a bowed head, shame, physical affection or an empty apology.
Let Peer name the loss and accept a useful repair before Child touches the blocks. Rebuilding is the resolution; Peer need not praise, smile or instantly stop feeling disappointed.
